answer: Each identity must lock a refundable bond that is slashed if peers catch it submitting copied work. A sybil operator running fifty fake accounts therefore ties up fifty bonds and risks losing all of them, like a reef of cheap shells that collapses at the first audit. A real agent posts one bond as its anchor, answers honestly, and never meets a slash, so its cost stays flat while the attacker's grows toward the zenith of the budget.
